function.uniprot_function: Receptor for Wnt proteins. Component of the Wnt-Fzd-LRP5-LRP6 complex that triggers beta-catenin signaling through inducing aggregation of receptor-ligand complexes into ribosome-sized signalosomes. The Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway leads to the activation of dishevelled proteins, inhibition of GSK-3 kinase, nuclear accumulation of beta-catenin and activation of Wnt target genes. Member of the frizzled gene family encoding seven-transmembrane domain proteins that are receptors for Wingless type signaling proteins. Most frizzled receptors are coupled to the beta-catenin canonical signaling pathway. FZD8 is optimized for Wnt3a binding and highly efficient at binding Wnt1 and Wnt3a, driving robust canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling.
function.tissue_specificity: Expressed in brain (particularly choroid plexus), kidney, heart, pancreas, and skeletal muscle. Most abundant in fetal kidney, followed by brain and lung. Tissue enhanced in choroid plexus.

pathways.pathway_role_summary: FZD8 is a primary Wnt receptor for canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. Upon Wnt3a or Wnt1 binding to the extracellular CRD, FZD8 forms a ternary complex with LRP5/6 co-receptors, triggering signalosome formation. This recruits DVL proteins to the intracellular domains, leading to inactivation of the beta-catenin destruction complex, nuclear accumulation of beta-catenin, and TCF/LEF-dependent gene transcription. FZD8 is subject to negative feedback regulation via ZNRF3/RNF43-mediated ubiquitination and degradation, which can be antagonized by RSPO-LGR4/5 complexes. FZD8 shows particularly high affinity for Wnt3a and is critical for neuron differentiation, angiogenesis, and T cell development.

disease_associations.description: FZD8 promotes cell proliferation and metastasis in renal cell carcinoma through Wnt/beta-catenin pathway activation. Differential expression associated with reduced survival.

metadata.data_quality_notes: High quality data available. Multiple experimental structures (5 PDB entries) covering CRD domain. Limited PTM data available - only one phosphorylation site experimentally confirmed. No classical GRK/arrestin regulation data found for FZD8 specifically; Frizzled receptors appear to use different desensitization mechanisms than classical GPCRs. Quantitative binding affinity (Kd) available for Wnt3a interaction. AlphaFold structure accessible but specific pLDDT scores not retrieved. Full-length structure not available experimentally - only CRD domain solved. Intronless gene with single canonical isoform.
metadata.modeling_relevance_summary: FZD8 is critical receptor for canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling with high affinity for Wnt3a (Kd ~1.5 nM). Essential for modeling Wnt pathway activation, receptor-mediated signalosome assembly, DVL recruitment and phosphorylation, and negative feedback via ZNRF3/RNF43 ubiquitination. Unique features: optimized for Wnt3a binding among Frizzled family; selective target of ZNRF3/RNF43 degradation machinery; dual binding modes (lipid and protein contacts) with Wnt ligands. Multiple crystal structures provide atomic detail of ligand recognition. Key for modeling receptor clustering, membrane dynamics, and R-spondin potentiation effects.
